entities.summary:
Infante Henry of Castile, called the Senator, was a Castilian infante, the fourth son of Ferdinand III of Castile by his first wife, Beatrice of Swabia. Born in 1255 in the Kingdom of Castile, Henry was groomed for a life of military service and governance from an early age. He played a significant role in the politics of the Iberian Peninsula during the late 13th century, often acting as a mediator between his father and other nobles.

Henry's life was marked by several key events, including his participation in the Battle of Las Navas de Tolosa in 1212, where Castilian forces defeated the Moorish army, securing a major victory for Christian forces in the Iberian Peninsula. He also played a crucial role in the signing of the Treaty of Zamora in 1217, which established a fragile peace between Castile and the Moorish kingdom of Granada.

Despite his relatively minor status compared to his more famous siblings, Henry's legacy lived on through his descendants, who would go on to shape the course of Castilian history. His influence can also be seen in the development of the Principality of Asturias, which he helped to establish as a key player in the politics of the Iberian Peninsula.

Henry's significance extends beyond his own lifetime, as he played a key role in the transition from the medieval to the early modern period in the Iberian Peninsula. His actions and decisions had a lasting impact on the region's politics, culture, and society, cementing his place as one of the lesser-known but still important figures of the Castilian infantes.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Infante Henry of Castile played a significant role in the politics of the Iberian Peninsula during the late 13th century, contributing to the signing of the Treaty of Zamora and the development of the Principality of Asturias. His legacy lived on through his descendants, who shaped the course of Castilian history for centuries to come.
